items.title: Roblox launches creator program for devs to bring games to its platform for free
items.excerpt: Roblox opens a creator program that ports existing mobile, PC and console games to its platform for free, using AI-assisted conversion tools to cut porting cost, with developers keeping IP ownership. Starting with a limited set of developers and games.
items.rationale: New platform program with direct action for studios: free AI-assisted porting to Roblox, IP retained. GamesIndustry.biz chosen over the Game*Spark version of the same story.

items.title: Stellar Blade: Blood Rain is "handmade from start to finish" after AI music video backlash, Shift Up boss says – but, uh, the devs are still using AI
items.excerpt: At G-STAR/G-CON 2026, SHIFT UP CEO Kim Hyung-tae made "handmade from start to finish" the studio's new principle for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain after the AI music-video backlash, while saying AI stays essential in development.
items.rationale: A major studio sets a public human-made principle after backlash yet keeps AI in the pipeline. Only card from the SHIFT UP cluster (GamesRadar+ chosen over Game*Spark, 아이뉴스24 and 4Gamer).

items.title: [지스타 2026] 코에이 테크모 "AI로 품질 검사 효율화…게임의 재미는 사람이"
items.excerpt: Koei Tecmo's Shibata Kohei at G-STAR 2026: AI handles QA and inspection work, and the time saved goes into polish such as frame-by-frame action tuning. He says fun has to be designed by people.
items.rationale: Concrete studio practice from a major Japanese publisher: AI goes into QA/inspection and the time saved goes into polish. It also brings a Korean outlet into the set.

items.title: Ex-Take Two boss believes that attitudes towards AI in game development will change for the better: 'We are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI'
items.excerpt: A former Take-Two executive argues player hostility to AI in games will fade once one breakout title proves its worth, comparing it to Toy Story's role in CG animation.
items.rationale: An industry veteran's counterpoint to the handmade trend, which frames this week's player-acceptance debate. This is a fresh statement, not a reaction to a story we already ran.

items.title: Principal Venture Partners’ Songyee Yoon on AI-native games, human creativity and gaming’s new rivals | GamesBeat Next 2026
items.excerpt: Former NCSoft president Songyee Yoon at GamesBeat Next 2026: AI-native games, where human creativity still matters, and how gaming's playbook will shape the next wave of AI companies.
items.rationale: A separate GamesBeat Next session from the 11-13 AI-native development panel, with a former NCSoft leader's view on AI-native games and creative roles. Fifth distinct outlet.
